findings.issue: Whole dashboard is still hidden behind the mandatory 'Logg på med Apple' wall. Sign-in fails with 'Kunne ikke starte Apple-innlogging (AUTHENTICATION_FAILED)' and there is no fallback/skip — no masthead, agenda, events, or 'Dette dekker vi' section render at all. The product's core promise (a calm scannable agenda) is completely invisible.
Same as 375px: only the Apple sign-in card and AUTHENTICATION_FAILED error are visible; no dashboard content renders.

Same as smaller widths: only the Apple sign-in card and AUTHENTICATION_FAILED error are visible; no dashboard content renders. At all three widths the #apple-sign-in-button area itself renders empty (CloudKit's own Sign-in-with-Apple control never appears) — once auth setup fails there is no visible interactive control to retry, only text instructing to reload the page or open DevTools.

notes: Unchanged repeat of the 2026-07-27/28 findings: the gate is a deliberate owner decision (documented inline in index.html around the auth-gate markup — 'eier-beslutning 21.07', body.gated hides all content until Sign in with Apple succeeds). `git log --since=2026-07-28 -- docs/index.html docs/js/icloud-sync.js docs/js/icloud-config.js docs/css/base.css` shows only the large self-repair commit (627a130) that restored a batch of previously untracked/missing repo files (workflows, skills, base.css itself as a 'new file' in git, etc.) — a repo-hygiene fix, not a change to the auth-gate markup, logic, or CSS rules. The gate text/behaviour is byte-identical to the prior run.

Could not assess ANY of the correctness/layout checklist (match name truncation, streaming channel/foreign-broadcaster check, times, flags/crests, must-see accent, header/footer alignment) at any width — everything behind the auth gate is unreachable without a successful Apple sign-in, and this screenshot harness has no network path to Apple's CloudKit web services.

The gate screen itself (wordmark, tagline, lead copy, error text) remains well laid out at all three widths: text wraps cleanly, no horizontal overflow, no clipping, calm and centered, single amber accent on the colon — same visual quality as the prior two runs.

Flagging high again (not escalating further) purely because it means visual QA cannot verify the actual product at all, run after run, in this offline harness — this is the same standing gap noted in the last two checks, not a new regression. A human should confirm whether real signed-in users in production see the dashboard fine (this may be purely an artifact of the no-network screenshot environment) and whether the empty sign-in-button-on-failure state (medium finding above) also occurs for real users whose CloudKit auth fails (e.g. Safari private browsing / blocked third-party cookies), since that would be a genuine dead end with no retry control.
